command:
set -eo pipefail
export PATH=/opt/conda/bin:$PATH
export TMPDIR=/tmp HOME=/tmp LC_ALL=C
cd /tmp
ls -l /tmp/tiger.zip

python3 -u - <<'PYEOF' > smoke-check.txt 2>&1 || { cat smoke-check.txt; exit 1; }
import sys, time, warnings
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")
import numpy as np
import geopandas as gpd
from pyproj import Geod
from libpysal.weights import Rook
from esda.moran import Moran
import statsmodels.api as sm
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression

fail = []
def check(label, ok, detail):
    print(f"{label:30s} {detail}")
    if not ok: fail.append(label)
def obs(label, detail):
    print(f"{label:30s} {detail}   [observation]")

import libpysal, esda, sklearn, statsmodels, shapely, pyproj
obs("versions", f"geopandas {gpd.__version__} shapely {shapely.__version__} "
                f"pyproj {pyproj.__version__} libpysal {libpysal.__version__} "
                f"esda {esda.__version__} sklearn {sklearn.__version__} "
                f"statsmodels {statsmodels.__version__}")

t0 = time.time()
g = gpd.read_file("/tmp/tiger.zip")
t_read = time.time() - t0
check("counties_read", len(g) == 3235,
      f"{len(g)} features  want exactly 3235 (TIGER2024 county file)")
check("crs_is_nad83", g.crs.to_epsg() == 4269,
      f"EPSG:{g.crs.to_epsg()}  want 4269 (NAD83 geographic, as TIGER ships)")
nvert = int(sum(len(p.exterior.coords) if p.geom_type == "Polygon"
                else sum(len(q.exterior.coords) for q in p.geoms)
                for p in g.geometry))
obs("exterior_vertices", f"{nvert:,} read in {t_read:.1f}s")

# ---- reproduce Census's own published areas ---------------------------------------
# ALAND + AWATER are Census's computed land and water areas in m^2, shipped in the same
# .dbf as the geometry. Recomputing from the polygons is a reproduction, not a
# measurement -- and it only works if the area is computed the way they computed it.
pub = (g["ALAND"].astype("int64") + g["AWATER"].astype("int64")).values
geod = Geod(ellps="WGS84")
t1 = time.time()
geo_area = np.array([abs(geod.geometry_area_perimeter(p)[0]) for p in g.geometry])
t_geod = time.time() - t1
rel = np.abs(geo_area - pub) / pub
# The residual is Census's own precision, not a fitted band: areas are published as
# integer m^2 on counties of order 1e9 m^2, and the observed median is 5e-08.
check("geodesic_area_vs_census", rel.max() < 1e-5,
      f"max rel err {rel.max():.3e} (median {np.median(rel):.3e}) over {len(g)} "
      f"counties  want < 1e-5")
check("total_area_conserved",
      abs(geo_area.sum() - pub.sum()) / pub.sum() < 1e-6,
      f"sum rel err {abs(geo_area.sum()-pub.sum())/pub.sum():.3e}  "
      f"({pub.sum():,} m^2 published)  want < 1e-6")

# The same areas through two projected CRSs, to show that the agreement above is a
# statement about the METHOD and not about geopandas. Observations, not assertions:
# Mercator's area distortion is a mathematical certainty, not a property of this build.
for nm, epsg in (("Albers equal-area 5070", 5070), ("Web Mercator 3857", 3857)):
    a = g.to_crs(epsg).area.values
    r = np.abs(a - pub) / pub
    obs(f"  via {nm}", f"median rel err {np.median(r):.3e}  max {r.max():.3e}")

# ---- contiguity weights: conservation, on real geometry --------------------------
# Contiguity needs land neighbours, so drop the island states and territories (AK, HI,
# AS, GU, MP, PR, VI) rather than carry 126 features with no neighbours.
ISLANDS = ["02", "15", "60", "66", "69", "72", "78"]
conus = g[~g.STATEFP.isin(ISLANDS)].reset_index(drop=True)
check("conus_subset", len(conus) == 3109,
      f"{len(conus)} counties  want exactly 3109 (3235 minus {len(g)-3109} island/territory)")
t2 = time.time()
w = Rook.from_dataframe(conus, use_index=False)
t_w = time.time() - t2
obs("rook_build", f"{t_w:.1f}s for {w.n} polygons, mean {w.s0/w.n:.3f} neighbours")
# Shared-edge contiguity is symmetric by construction, so the directed-link count must be
# even and is exactly twice the number of shared edges. Integer identities, no band.
check("weights_symmetric",
      all(i in w.neighbors[j] for i in w.neighbors for j in w.neighbors[i]),
      f"every link reciprocated over {w.n} polygons")
check("links_even", w.s0 % 2 == 0,
      f"s0 = {w.s0:.0f} = 2 x {int(w.s0//2)} shared edges  want even")
check("no_islands", len(w.islands) == 0,
      f"{len(w.islands)} polygons with no neighbour  want 0 after dropping {ISLANDS}")
w.transform = "r"
# Row-standardising makes each row sum to 1, so the total must equal the row count
# exactly -- a conservation check on the transform itself.
check("row_standardised_sums_to_n", abs(w.s0 - w.n) < 1e-9,
      f"s0 = {w.s0:.6f} after row-standardisation  want exactly n = {w.n}")

# ---- Moran's I: an invariance, which is exact ------------------------------------
y = np.log10(conus["ALAND"].astype("float64").values)
m1 = Moran(y, w, permutations=0)
# I is a ratio of covariance to variance of the SAME centred variable, so it is invariant
# under any non-degenerate affine transform -- including a sign flip. Not a band: the two
# numbers must be bit-identical, and an implementation that normalised wrongly would not
# be. This is the strongest available statement about a statistic with no closed-form
# reference value.
m2 = Moran(3.7 * y + 112.5, w, permutations=0)
m3 = Moran(-y, w, permutations=0)
obs("morans_I", f"{m1.I:.12f} for log10(ALAND) over {w.n} counties")
check("moran_affine_invariant", m1.I == m2.I,
      f"I(y) == I(3.7y + 112.5) exactly: |diff| = {abs(m1.I-m2.I):.2e}")
check("moran_sign_invariant", m1.I == m3.I,
      f"I(y) == I(-y) exactly: |diff| = {abs(m1.I-m3.I):.2e}")
# The expectation under the null is -1/(n-1) in closed form.
check("moran_expectation", abs(m1.EI - (-1.0/(w.n-1))) < 1e-15,
      f"EI = {m1.EI:.12f}  want -1/(n-1) = {-1.0/(w.n-1):.12f}")

# ---- three OLS implementations on the same real data ----------------------------
X = np.log10(conus["AWATER"].astype("float64").values + 1.0)
ols = sm.OLS(y, sm.add_constant(X)).fit()
sk = LinearRegression().fit(X.reshape(-1, 1), y)
beta, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(np.c_[np.ones_like(X), X], y, rcond=None)
spread = max(abs(ols.params[0] - sk.intercept_), abs(ols.params[1] - sk.coef_[0]),
             abs(ols.params[0] - beta[0]), abs(ols.params[1] - beta[1]))
obs("ols_fit", f"intercept {ols.params[0]:.9f} slope {ols.params[1]:.9f} "
               f"R2 {ols.rsquared:.9f}")
# statsmodels (QR/pinv), scikit-learn (LAPACK gelsd) and the normal equations solved by
# lstsq are three routes to one least-squares solution. On a well-conditioned real design
# they must agree to double precision, so the tolerance is conditioning, not taste.
check("three_ols_agree", spread < 1e-12,
      f"max pairwise |diff| across statsmodels / sklearn / lstsq = {spread:.2e}  "
      f"want < 1e-12")

obs("wall_geodesic_area", f"{t_geod:.1f}s over {nvert:,} vertices")
obs("wall_rook_weights", f"{t_w:.1f}s")

if fail:
    print("FAILED: " + ", ".join(fail)); sys.exit(1)
PYEOF
cat smoke-check.txt
echo "SMOKE CHECK PASSED"
